Every player can have several action bars with 50 action buttons per bar. For every hotkey preset, players can configure separate action bars. By right-clicking on an action button, you will have different options depending whether you like to assign a spell, an object or a text, or if you like to assign a hotkey to an action button.

Action buttons which are already in use have the additional option "Clear Action" which will delete an assigned action from this button. Action buttons are greyed out if they contain an object which you do not have with you or a spell which your character cannot use.

If the lock is open, you can easily assign or switch an action to an action button using "drag&drop". Hotkeys are bound to an action button, so they will not be moved this way. Items with a tier grant unique bonuses.

The bonus granted by an item's tier depends on its function, with higher tiers increasing the chance of triggering these effects:
• Weapons grant a chance to deal 60% more damage.
• Armors grant a chance to fully mitigate the damage from an attack.
• Helmets grant a chance to reduce all cooldowns during combat.
• Legs grant a chance to trigger Transcendence, turning your character into an avatar for a few seconds, providing damage reduction and enhanced critical hits.
• Boots amplify the effects of other tiered items.
The classification of an item defines its maximum tier.

• Items of classification 4 can be upgraded up to tier 10.
• Items of classification 3 can be upgraded up to tier 3.
• Items of classification 2 can be upgraded up to tier 2.
• Items of classification 1 can be upgraded up to tier 1.
• Items with no classification cannot be upgraded.

There are two chat modes for each hotkey preset: Chat On and Chat Off. You can find a small button that tells you which chat mode is currently active on the right side of the entry line of the chat console. Press this button to switch between the two chat modes. Of course, you can also set a hotkey to toggle between Chat On an Off.

  • Chat On
    In this mode, you will be able to write text in the entry line of the chat console. However, if you have assigned an action to a letter key, the action will be triggered.
  • Chat On*
    This is the temporary Chat On mode. In the default hotkey preset, the Return key switches between Chat Off and this mode. If the chat mode is off and you press this hotkey, it temporarily activates the chat mode so that you can write one message in the console. As soon as you press Return to send the message, your chat mode will be set to Chat Off again so that you can continue walking with WASD, for example.
  • Chat Off
    In this mode, you will not be able to write any text in the entry line of the console, but you can use your predefined hotkeys to walk or cast spells, for example. You can assign functions to all keys of your keyboard, e.g. walk with WASD.

If a character is afflicted with agony, they will continuously take damage over time. There is no way to cure, block or resist this effect - the only option is to endure it until it fades.

Sometimes, creatures inflict heavy wounds on your character that bleed for a certain period of time. While losing blood, your character becomes increasingly weak and loses health points over time. Those who know the "Cure Bleeding" spell are fortunate, as they can instantly force the gaping wound to close.

This is a harmful effect of the fire damage type that causes your character to lose hit points over an extended period of time. Until it ends, a searing flame will appear on your character at regular intervals. The damage dealt by the fire depends on its source. Druids have the magical ability to cure any burning.

Characters who are hungry regenerate hit points and mana more slowly. To fill your character's stomach, look for something edible, such as an apple, bread, or ham. There are plenty of things in Tibia that your character can eat. Check out stores, search bushes, bake your own bread or cake, or defeat creatures to find some delicacies.

Have your health potions and healing spells ready whenever a creature curses you. If your character is affected by this special condition of the death damage type, a black cloud will literally hang over their head. For a considerable time, they will lose an increasing amount of hit points at regular intervals. Only paladins, as masters of holy magic, are able to cure a character of a curse.

If your character is marked as dazzled, a holy light has just struck with pitiless force. Similar to being electrified, your character will lose a decreasing amount of hit points a few times. This condition, caused by the holy damage type, has no remedy - your only options are to wait it out or seek healing from a nearby priest.

Tibia features a special underwater area. Since no one can survive without fresh air, characters will take damage if they walk underwater without the proper equipment. The only way to survive is to leave the water quickly or equip a life-saving diving helmet.

Taverns in Tibia are popular gathering places where many adventurers enjoy relaxing after their wearisome travels with a pint of cool beer. However, Tibian beer is quite strong, so don't be surprised if your character has trouble walking in a straight line for a while.

Electrified is a condition of the energy damage type that causes prolonged hit point loss, similar to the burning condition caused by fire. A flash of electrical energy will appear on your character at regular intervals, dealing damage each time it occurs. As with burning, only druids have the power to end this unpleasant condition using the "Cure Electrification" spell.

Feared is a condition that certain monsters can cast on you. If you are feared, you temporarily lose control of your character. During this time, your character will run away from the creature that caused the fear. In addition, you cannot cast spells or use any items.

If your character is part of an active guild war, they will receive a protection zone block when attacking enemies. Kills against the same enemy count up to five times within 24 hours. Characters not involved in the war cannot heal or buff your character if they were recently damaged by a member of the opposing guild.

Characters affected by a logout block cannot log out safely. It occurs when engaging in or being affected by combat actions like attacking, casting offensive spells, or taking damage. The block lasts 60 seconds from the last violent act. Killing another player extends the block to 15 minutes. Wait until the icon disappears before logging out to avoid leaving your character vulnerable.
You are protected by a magic shield

Another positive spell effect, magic shields protect characters from losing hit points while active by reducing their mana instead. However, if a character’s mana is reduced to zero, any further damage will be deducted from their hit points as usual.

A Monk’s active Virtue empowers each vocation with a unique bonus that strengthens its primary role - such as healer, damage dealer, tank, or spellcaster - when fighting together in a party. A monk only receives the respective vocation effect while serene.

Some creatures or spells may slow your character down. Until the effect ends or is dispelled by healing magic, your character will move much more slowly than usual. However, all other actions - such as casting spells - can still be performed normally.
You have attacked an unmarked player

A character marked with a white skull has recently attacked or killed an unmarked character. This mark is visible to all players and remains active as long as the logout block is in effect. If the character continues to perform offensive actions while marked, the duration of the white skull, the logout block and the protection zone block will be extended.
You may be attacked by other players

This skull is somewhat special because it is not visible to all players on the screen. You will only see it if your character was attacked or damaged by another character while your own character was marked with a skull. This indicates your right to defend yourself, even while being marked.
Killing a character with a yellow skull does not count as a "unjustified" kill, just like any other kill of a marked character. Similar to a white skull, a yellow skull remains active as long as the logout block is in effect. If the character continues to perform offensive actions while marked with a yellow skull, the duration of the skull, the logout block and the connected protection zone block will be extended.
You have excessively killed unmarked players

A character with a black skull has committed too many unjustified kills while already marked with a red skull. While marked, the character drops all items upon death, cannot attack unmarked characters and cannot use the expert mode Red Fist. They receive full damage in PvP and will revive with only 40 hit points and 0 mana. The black skull lasts 45 days and is reset if the character continues to gain unjustified points during this time.
You are a member of a party

While in a party, your character cannot accidentally harm party members with any attacks, such as area spells. Party members can also benefit from shared experience and access to certain party-exclusive spells.
You have killed too many unmarked players

A red skull marks a character who has killed or assisted in killing too many unmarked players. While marked, the character will drop all items upon death, even with blessings or an Amulet of Loss. The red skull lasts 30 days and resets if further unjustified kills occur during this time.
You may suffer revenge from your former victim

An orange skull is only visible to the character who was killed unjustified and to the killer. It appears when your character has been killed unjustified by another player and lasts for 7 days. If you kill a character marked with an orange skull, the kill does not count as unjustified. However, attacking them still results in a yellow skull and a protection zone block. The orange skull disappears either after 7 days or once you have taken revenge for each unjustified kill received within that time.

This condition of the earth damage type can be caused by spells or certain monsters. The total damage dealt by poisons can vary greatly, but any poisoning can be easily removed by using the "Cure Poison" spell or the "Cure Poison Rune".

A protection zone block is always accompanied by a logout block. If your character attacks another character first, they will not only be unable to log out but also unable to enter any protection zones. However, there is no protection zone block when you attack a member of your own party.

Just like in a protection zone, characters cannot perform any aggressive actions. In addition, they are safe from attacks by creatures or other characters.
